specs.source_title: Introduction to Bambu Lab Build Plates | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.locator: Build Plate Types › Cool Plate SuperTack tab › paragraph 1
specs.quote: The Cool Plate SuperTack features a finely textured surface that approaches a smooth, glossy finish.
specs.note: Value worded from the quote. The store page says the coating gives the print's bottom surface "a smooth and matte texture" (the print, not the plate): no conflict.

specs.source_title: Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.locator: Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack › paragraph 1
specs.quote: Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack is made by coating a spring steel sheet with SuperTack
specs.note: Value worded from the quote. The store page row "Material | Specially Designed Coating / Spring Steel Plate" (part.material, verified on the page) says the same in other words; it is not overwritten.

specs.source_title: Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.locator: Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack › paragraph 1
specs.quote: Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack is made by coating a spring steel sheet with SuperTack and is suitable for PLA and PETG filaments.
specs.test_condition: PLA and PETG only (plates wiki: "This plate is designed only for printing PLA and PETG. Using any other materials may damage the surface coating.")
specs.note: Agrees with the plates wiki (Cool Plate SuperTack tab, Note) and the store page feature bullet "Designed for PLA and PETG". Exceptions the same sources give: Bambu PLA Silk is not recommended; printing PLA/PETG support may damage the plate (print a raft layer first).

specs.source_title: Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.locator: Notes › Filament printing recommendations › bullets 1–2
specs.quote: Do not print with TPU filament, as it will damage the build plate. … we do not recommend using Bambu PLA Silk material on the SuperTack build plate.
specs.test_condition: TPU: do not print (damages the plate). Bambu PLA Silk: not recommended (its strong adhesion may damage printed models)
specs.note: The store page Considerations say the same ("Do NOT print with TPU filament …"; "we do not recommend using Bambu PLA Silk material …"). For third-party PLA Silk both sources say to select the Generic PLA Silk preset in Bambu Studio and evaluate compatibility.

specs.source_title: Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack Series (store page)
specs.locator: Product Specifications › row 3 (Surface Temperature Resistance)
specs.quote: Surface Temperature Resistance | Up to 120℃
specs.test_condition: Surface temperature resistance of the plate
specs.note: The registry has no synonym for "Surface Temperature Resistance", so the page row stays x.surface_temperature_resistance ("Up to 120℃"); this row types the same fact. Same value: agrees. The wiki pages give no temperature limit.

specs.value: Consumable part, will degrade over time
specs.source_title: Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack Series (store page)
specs.locator: Description › Considerations › bullet 5, sentence 1
specs.quote: Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack is considered a consumable part, which will degrade over time.
specs.note: Value worded from the quote. Only the first sentence of the bullet: the two warranty sentences after it are withheld by the page builder as owner-only manufacturer_terms.warranty_note (L-19) and are not curated.

documents.title: How to print Support for PLA/PETG with Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack
documents.text: How to print Support for PLA/PETG with Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack
documents.note: Linked from both wiki pages (SuperTack wiki "refer to this wiki"; plates wiki Further Reading); not cached, so not read for specs.

notes: Sizes per printer come from the SuperTack wiki "Compatible Models" table (350*320 mm H2D / H2S; 330*320 mm H2C / A2L; 256*256 mm X2D / P2S / P1 Series / X1 Series / A1); the plates wiki's general dimensions table gives the same rows. Stored as product.length/product.width per Printer Model option. They agree with the store page's "Usable Print Size" row.

Material: the page row "Specially Designed Coating / Spring Steel Plate" (part.material, verified) stays; the wiki's "coating a spring steel sheet with SuperTack" says the same, so the coating name is curated as part.surface_treatment instead of rewording part.material.
Thickness: only the store page gives it ("Coating - 0.05mm / Steel Plate - 0.4mm"); left to the page row (unverified; its value_num 0.05 is the coating layer). No curated thickness.

Packaging Size / Packaging Weight: the page labels its segments by printer groups ("X1C/P1P/P1S/A1/P2S/X2D", "H2D/H2S", "H2C/A2L"), not by the option values, and the "+ Mag-Alloy Scraper" bundle options share the same Printer Model values with no figures of their own, so scoping the plate-only box per Printer Model option would also attribute it to the bundles. Not curated; the page rows stay unverified at product scope. No net weight is published.

Generations: the SuperTack wiki says the 256×256 mm plate exists as the original and the SuperTack Pro (updated QR code identification); the store page offers "Cool Plate SuperTack" options for X2D / P2S / A1 / P1 Series / X1 Series and "Cool Plate SuperTack Pro" options for A2L / H2C / H2S / H2D, and does not say which 256 mm generation it ships. No generation-specific spec or relation is written; the plate-detection advice is kept in the printer relations' notes and as the page's variant.note rows.

A1 mini: the SuperTack wiki's Installation Steps pictures include an "A1 mini" row, but its Compatible Models table, the plates wiki and the store page offer no A1 mini size, so no A1 mini relation is written.
Marketing prose not stored as numbers: "less than 20% adhesion loss after 300 prints" (test with PLA Basic on the A1) and the energy-saving claims.

Bed temperatures (PLA 45℃ on the store comparison table, 40 °C in the plates wiki; PETG 55–60 °C for the 2nd-generation plate, around 65 °C on the X/P series) have no registry key for a plate (print_settings.* applies to filament only); they are kept in the material relations' notes. Removal aid "heat the plate on the heatbed to 50°C" is a usage step on the page.
Glue: "SuperTack provides good adhesion without adhesive", so no requires relation is written.

No in-the-box list: neither the store page nor the wiki gives an official packing list. The "+ Mag-Alloy Scraper" options name a bundled scraper in the option text only; no includes relation (outside the curated relation kinds) and no in_the_box entry are written.
The wiki video https://public-cdn.bblmw.com/wiki/accessory/Bambu-Cool-Plate-SuperTack-en.mp4 is on a host outside the document allow-list, so it is not listed as a document.
